subject: Private VPC observability export runbook / SIEM handoff kickoff
snippet: Kickoff for VPC/on-prem observability exports and SIEM mapping; runbook draft and next steps.
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <secops@enterpriseco.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: lena.ortiz@enterpriseco.com
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2024 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Observability exports from our VPC -> SIEM (hit list + formats)

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. We need to firm up the handoff for our private deployment (VPC) so our SIEM team can ingest logs and traces with the right fields. High-level asks: 

- What exact log/metric formats will Redwood's private forwarder emit (JSON lines, syslog, HEC)?
- Can we get a sample field mapping CSV so our SIEM mappings are ready before go-live?
- Tracing hooks: what span attributes do you preserve (service.name, pipeline_id, request_id, model_version)?
- Any recommended network egress rules and ports for the forwarder when running in a restricted subnet?

I attached our current SIEM mapping template to this thread (enterpriseco-siem-field-mapping.csv). Can someone at Redwood provide a short runbook we can use in our runbook repo? We want to validate retention and custody for audit.

Proposed timeline: runbook draft by 11/12, validation test week of 11/18.

Appreciate it — let me know who to loop in on the Redwood side.

Best,
Alex
Security Engineer, EnterpriseCo

Attachments: enterpriseco-siem-field-mapping.csv (application/csv)

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <secops@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2024 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability exports from our VPC -> SIEM (hit list + formats)

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly and Diego from Private Deployments + Observability to draft a runbook and sample outputs. Quick answers inline then we'll follow up with artifacts: 

- Formats: our forwarder supports JSON-lines (newline-delimited JSON) and Splunk HEC. We also have an optional syslog shims for legacy collectors. Preference for HEC when possible because it preserves event attributes and batching.
- Field mapping: Diego will attach a CSV mapping to match your template.
- Tracing hooks: we emit span attributes including service.name, redwood.model, request_id, model_version, routing_policy, and trace.cold_start. We keep a stable span name (inference.request) to make correlation simpler.
- Network: outbound only (TCP 443) to configured SIEM endpoints; mutual TLS is supported for HEC. Allow ephemeral egress to our private-forwarder IPs during onboarding if you need short-lived tunnels.

We will produce a short 2–3 page runbook draft that includes: expected outputs, sample events, auth (HEC token / mTLS), retention considerations, and troubleshooting steps. I can do the first draft by EOD 11/12; Diego will provide the mapping CSV and an evidence diagram.

Next steps: Diego — can you paste the sample JSON event and attach the runbook draft? Kimberly — please add any compliance notes (retention, audit log hooks).

Thanks,
Chloe
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 6 Nov 2024 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability exports from our VPC -> SIEM (hit list + formats)

Hi all — attaching what I promised. Key points up-front:

- Attached CSV (enterpriseco-siem-field-mapping.csv) maps Redwood event keys -> EnterpriseCo SIEM fields and includes notes for truncation and PII scrubbing.
- Sample event (JSON-lines) below for quick verification. We include stable request_id and model_version, and we add a redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit boolean when applicable.

Sample event (one line):
{
  "timestamp": "2024-11-06T15:22:11.123Z",
  "level": "info",
  "service.name": "redwood-inference-forwarder",
  "request_id": "req_8b3f2c",
  "model_version": "gptq-4x-1.2.0",
  "redwood.model": "rw-large-13b",
  "redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit": false,
  "msg": "inference completed (tokens: 24, latency_ms: 112)"
}

- For traces we emit OTLP-compatible spans and set resource.service.name = "redwood-inference". Span attributes preserved: request_id, pipeline_id (when present), model_version, routing_policy. We recommend correlating logs via request_id / trace_id.

- Network recommendations: port 443 outbound only; for HEC we recommend mTLS + IP allowlist. When running in highly restricted subnets, deploy the forwarder as a sidecar with an internal egress proxy (we provided a diagram).

I've also attached a draft runbook (redwood-private-obsv-runbook-draft.md) and a lightweight VPC evidence diagram (vpc-evidence-diagram.png). Chloe — I left a short troubleshooting section covering: dropped batches (increase forwarder buffer), HEC token errors (clock skew), and sampled trace discrepancies.

Diego
Observability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: enterpriseco-siem-field-mapping.csv, redwood-private-obsv-runbook-draft.md, vpc-evidence-diagram.png

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, Alex Rivera <secops@enterpriseco.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Nov 2024 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability exports from our VPC -> SIEM (hit list + formats)

Thanks — this looks good. A couple of compliance notes for your auditors, Alex: 

- Retention: the forwarder can be configured to buffer up to 14 days locally (configurable) but we recommend you set SIEM retention to meet your policy; Redwood does not retain customer telemetry for private deployments unless explicitly enabled.
- Audit logging: we capture request-level audit events (config changes, forwarder restarts, key rotations). Those can be exported to the same HEC endpoint; recommend separating audit stream into a distinct index for search controls.
- Evidence package: for SOC 2 requests, we can provide a signed packet with export configs and attestations; please open an evidence request ticket (OPS-1428) and we'll assemble artifacts.

Chloe — if you want, I'll add a short appendix to Diego's runbook covering: how to demonstrate custody during audits and a sample itemized evidence checklist.

Kimberly
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
